target: Fazia calor e o sol brilhava quando saímos de casa.
english: It was hot and the sun was shining when we left the house.
tip: Background description in imperfeito: 'fazia calor e o sol brilhava' sets the scene for 'saímos' (event).

target: Eu fiz uma besteira enorme.
english: I made a huge mistake.
tip: fazer besteira means to do something dumb; besteira comes from besta, beast.

target: Eu disse que não podia ir.
english: I said I couldn't go.
tip: disse covers both 'I said' and 'he/she said'; only the pronoun (eu vs ele) tells them apart.

target: Eu fiz as pazes com ela.
english: I made peace with her.
tip: 'Fazer as pazes' means to make up/reconcile after a fight. Always plural: 'as pazes,' never 'a paz' in this expression.

target: Vocês foram felizes nessa decisão.
english: You were happy with that decision.
tip: foram means both 'went' and 'were'; the adjective after it, foram felizes, marks it as 'were' here.

target: Vocês disseram algo para ele?
english: Did you say anything to him?
tip: vocês is the plural 'you' everywhere; Portugal's older vós still shows up in writing but is gone from speech.

target: Vocês viram aquele programa na TV?
english: Did you see that TV show?
tip: viram means 'saw'; add an e and you get vieram, 'came'. One letter separates them.

target: Ela veio de avião do Recife.
english: She came by plane from Recife.
tip: 'Vir' (to come) → 'veio' (he/she came). Don't confuse with 'viu' from 'ver' (to see).

target: Ela disse que vai pensar no assunto.
english: She said she'll think about it.
tip: Reported speech keeps the original tense: disse que vai is 'said she will', where English shifts to 'would'.

target: Eu vi um acidente na estrada.
english: I saw an accident on the road.
tip: vi is 'I saw', as in vi um acidente; don't mix it up with vim, 'I came'. One letter apart.

target: Ele pôs as chaves na mesa.
english: He put the keys on the table.
tip: pôs is the past of pôr, 'put'; in casual Brazilian speech people reach for colocar instead (colocou).

target: O restaurante estava cheio quando chegamos.
english: The restaurant was full when we arrived.
tip: 'Estava cheio' (imperfeito, description) + 'chegamos' (perfeito, event). Scene + arrival pattern.

target: Eu soube que ela passou no concurso.
english: I heard she passed the civil service exam.
tip: 'Concurso' in Brazil refers to competitive civil service exams. Passing one is a huge achievement and guarantees a stable government job.

target: Nós comíamos pamonha na época da colheita.
english: We used to eat pamonha during harvest time.
tip: Pamonha is a traditional Brazilian snack made from fresh corn wrapped in corn husks. Very popular in the countryside and during festas juninas.

target: Nós trocamos a TV por uma maior.
english: We exchanged the TV for a bigger one.
tip: 'Por' for exchange/substitution: 'trocar A por B' = to exchange A for B.

target: Enquanto a gente jantava, ele contou a novidade.
english: While we were having dinner, he shared the news.
tip: 'Enquanto' (while) + imperfect for background action; the main event uses preterite.

target: Eu não sabia que ele estava aqui até que o vi.
english: I didn't know he was here until I saw him.
tip: 'Sabia' (imperfeito, state of not knowing) + 'vi' (perfeito, moment of seeing). Discovery interrupted a state.

target: Ela se arrependeu de não ter ido.
english: She regretted not having gone.
tip: 'Arrepender-se de' means 'to regret.' This verb is always reflexive in Portuguese – there's no non-reflexive form.

target: Eu te falei sobre isso ontem.
english: I told you about this yesterday.
tip: 'Te' is the object pronoun for 'tu/você' (informal). In Brazil, 'te' is used with 'você' even though grammatically it belongs to 'tu.'

target: A gente brincava de esconde-esconde.
english: We used to play hide and seek.
tip: brincar takes de before a game: brincava de esconde-esconde, literally 'played of' hide and seek.

target: Eu sonhava em morar no exterior.
english: I used to dream of living abroad.
tip: sonhar pairs with em, not de: sonhava em morar. English 'dream of' can push you to the wrong preposition.

target: Eu não te entendi, pode repetir?
english: I didn't understand you, can you repeat?
tip: 'Te' as direct object: 'não te entendi' = I didn't understand you. Pronoun before verb in negatives.

target: Ele me indicou um bom restaurante.
english: He suggested a good restaurant.
tip: indicar looks like 'indicate' but means recommend: me indicou um bom restaurante is 'suggested a good restaurant to me'.

target: Ele trabalhava num banco antes de mudar de área.
english: He used to work at a bank before switching fields.
tip: antes de takes an infinitive where English uses -ing: antes de mudar is 'before switching', not 'before to switch'.

target: Quem mandou essa mensagem?
english: Who sent this message?
tip: Portuguese questions use no do or did. Quem mandou is just Who sent, the plain past-tense verb carrying the question alone.

target: Eu me chamo Lucas.
english: My name is Lucas.
tip: 'Chamar-se' literally means 'to call oneself.' 'Me chamo Lucas' = I call myself Lucas. The most basic reflexive verb you'll learn.

target: Ele se orgulha dos filhos.
english: He's proud of his children.
tip: Orgulhar-se takes de for what you are proud of: orgulha dos filhos, where dos is de plus os.

target: A gente esperou por duas horas.
english: We waited for two hours.
tip: 'A gente' means we in speech but takes a third-person singular verb: esperou, never esperamos.

target: Sem que ninguém perceba, ele saiu.
english: Without anyone noticing, he left.
tip: sem que always takes the subjunctive: sem que ninguém perceba, where perceba is the subjunctive of perceber.

target: Para variar, ele chegou atrasado.
english: For a change, he arrived late.
tip: 'Para variar' is a set phrase meaning for a change, usually said with irony about something predictable.
